subject: Sandbox access, routing options & rate-cap plan for FinLytics pilot
messages:
From: Kai Brooks <kai@finlytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-07T20:15:00Z
Subject: Follow-up from today’s demo — hosting path questions

Thanks Marcus — great walkthrough this morning. A couple quick follow-ups from our side as we finalize the pilot scope: 

1) For our initial pilot we want the simplest path: can you confirm whether the Hosted API will meet our data residency and PII handling constraints for US customers? We don’t need on-prem for pilot unless required.

2) Can you send the sandbox endpoints + token provisioning flow and recommended rate caps? Our expected traffic profile for a 4-week pilot: avg 10 req/s, 50 req/s peak bursts, typical prompt ~450 tokens, completions ~150 tokens.

3) Any docs you can share for SOC 2 attestation (cover page / articulation of scoping) would be helpful — procurement/security will want that before handing over live test data.

Thanks,
Kai Brooks
Head of Product, FinLytics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Kai Brooks <kai@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-07T22:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today’s demo — hosting path questions

Hi Kai — thanks for the detailed notes and for taking the time today. Recap + proposed sandbox plan below.

Short answers up front: Hosted API is the recommended path for your pilot (US region). It supports PII workflows under our standard DPA and we can limit data retention for pilot traffic. Private/Dedicated only recommended if you require VPC isolation or contractually required on-prem.

Proposed sandbox configuration (what we'll provision this week if you confirm):
- Two sandbox endpoints over HTTPS:
  - /v1/finlytics/low-latency — optimized routing for single-request latency (suitable for front-end UX).
  - /v1/finlytics/throughput — pooling/continuous-batching for back-office batch jobs.
- Token provisioning: ephemeral sandbox API key via console; rotateable every 7 days. We'll provide a short script to fetch keys.
- Rate caps (sandbox):
  - per-endpoint sustained: 12 req/s
  - burst window (5s): 60 req/s
  - per-account concurrent token limit: 10k tokens/sec (sandbox aggregate)
- Suggested pilot quotas: 1M tokens/week to start (we can scale up quickly).

Attachments: I’m attaching a one-page onboarding checklist that covers the console flows, endpoint URLs, example curl snippets, and the support contacts. (redwood-sandbox-onboarding-checklist.pdf)

Next steps I propose:
1) FinLytics confirms sandbox start date and primary security contact.
2) We share SOC 2 cover page + drive link (see Laura/Aditya cc’d).
3) We provision sandbox keys and give a short 30-min ops preflight call to validate traffic patterns.

If Hosted looks good after the pilot we can evaluate Dedicated capacity thresholds (we can do a cost estimate based on real token volumes).

—Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>; Kai Brooks <kai@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-08T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today’s demo — hosting path questions

Adding a quick note on billing and trial credits for the pilot:
- We can issue $10k in trial credits against Hosted usage for the 4-week pilot; credits apply to per-token usage only (not third-party storage).
- If FinLytics expects to exceed ~3M tokens/day sustained, we should evaluate a Reserved/Dedicated conversation early — helps keep unit cost predictable.
- Action for procurement: I’ll send a short trial-credit agreement to the HubSpot company record once Kai confirms the sandbox start date.

(Attachment: trial-credit-agreement.pdf — will send signed copy after procurement ack)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Ops, Redwood Inference
From: procurement@finlytics.com <procurement@finlytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-08T16:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today’s demo — hosting path questions

Marcus / Laura — thanks for the clear plan. A few items procurement/security need before we spin up sandbox with synthetic test data: 

- SOC 2 evidence: cover page + pointer to the SOC 2 report or AICPA folder. A cover page that explains in-scope systems and the date of the latest attestation is sufficient for this stage.
- Region confirmation: US-only is fine.
- Sandbox start: can you provision keys on Monday 2028-06-12? That gives our infra team one business day to add the test IP allowlist.

I’m copying security@finlytics.com for the SOC 2 artifacts.

Thanks — procurement@finlytics.com
